description.narrative:
Sverige stödjer Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) i genomförandet av programmet "Strengthening Access to Justice and Legal Protection for Refugees and Vulnerable Communities in Jordan". Insatsen uppgår till 25 000 000 SEK under två år, från den 1 juni 2026 till den 31 maj 2028. Mottagarland är Jordanien.
Det övergripande målet är att stärka förmågan hos flyktingar, särskilt syrier, och hos utsatta jordanier, i synnerhet kvinnor, barn och andra grupper som utestängs rättsligt, att utöva sina rättigheter och att minska deras rättsliga utsatthet. Programmet arbetar mot detta genom tre sammanhängande delmål.
Det första stärker tillgången till tillförlitlig rättslig information och hänvisningstjänster på lokal nivå. NRC och partnerorganisationerna genomför informationstillfällen om rättsliga frågor och tar fram digitalt material, samt stärker kapaciteten hos lokalt förankrade organisationer (community-based organisations, CBO) och frivilliga att ge korrekt information och trygga hänvisningar.
Det andra förbättrar tillgången till rättvisa genom individuell rättslig rådgivning och rättsligt biträde. Ärendena rör civilrättslig dokumentation, laglig vistelse, familjerättsliga frågor såsom äktenskap, födelseregistrering, vårdnad och förmynderskap, samt rättigheter till bostad, mark och egendom (housing, land and property, HLP), inklusive ärenden med gränsöverskridande inslag. Underlag som tas fram genom ärendehanteringen används för analys och dialog med myndigheter och andra skyldighetsbärare.
Det tredje stödjer Jordaniens justitieministerium i att institutionalisera, operationalisera och digitalisera förenklade domstolsförfaranden för mindre tvistemål, och stärker domares, advokaters och domstolspersonals förmåga att tillämpa dem enhetligt.
NRC genomför programmet tillsammans med Justice Centre for Legal Aid (JCLA), en jordansk rättshjälpsorganisation, som strategisk partner, och med minst fyra CBO som väljs ut under en inledande uppstartsfas. Verksamheten bedrivs i de norra och centrala guvernementen Irbid, Mafraq, Ajloun, Jarash, Balqa, Madaba, Amman och Zarqa.
Programmet riktar sig till 15 768 unika direkta deltagare, varav 61 procent är kvinnor och flickor, cirka 70 procent flyktingar och 30 procent utsatta jordanier, samt omkring 200 000 indirekta deltagare. Förväntade resultat omfattar ökad kunskap om rättigheter bland deltagarna, individer som får eller kan utöva sina rättigheter efter rättshjälp, lokalt förankrade organisationer som självständigt kan ge rättslig information och hänvisning, samt förenklade förfaranden för mindre tvistemål som formellt antas och tillämpas av justitieministeriet.

Sweden supports the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) in implementing the programme "Strengthening Access to Justice and Legal Protection for Refugees and Vulnerable Communities in Jordan". The contribution amounts to SEK 25,000,000 over two years, from 1 June 2026 to 31 May 2028. The recipient country is Jordan.
The overall objective is to strengthen the ability of refugees, particularly Syrians, and of vulnerable Jordanians, in particular women, children and other legally excluded groups, to exercise their rights and to reduce their legal vulnerability. The programme pursues this through three connected sub objectives.
The first strengthens access to reliable legal information and referral services at community level. NRC and its partners deliver legal information sessions and digital content, and build the capacity of community-based organisations (CBOs) and community volunteers to provide accurate information and safe referrals.
The second improves access to justice through individual legal counselling and legal assistance. Cases concern civil documentation, legal stay, family law matters such as marriage, birth registration, custody and guardianship, and housing, land and property (HLP) rights, including cases with a cross-border dimension. Evidence generated from casework is used for analysis and engagement with authorities and other duty bearers.
The third supports the Jordanian Ministry of Justice to institutionalise, operationalise and digitalise expedited court procedures for small claims cases, and strengthens the capacity of judges, lawyers and court staff to apply them consistently.
NRC implements the programme together with the Justice Centre for Legal Aid (JCLA), a Jordanian legal aid organisation, as strategic partner, and with at least four CBOs to be selected during an inception phase. Activities take place in the northern and central governorates of Irbid, Mafraq, Ajloun, Jarash, Balqa, Madaba, Amman and Zarqa.
The programme targets 15,768 unique direct participants, of whom 61 per cent are women and girls, around 70 per cent refugees and 30 per cent vulnerable Jordanians, and approximately 200,000 indirect participants. Expected results include increased knowledge of legal rights among participants, individuals obtaining or exercising their rights following legal aid, CBOs delivering legal information and referrals independently, and simplified small claims procedures formally adopted and applied by the Ministry of Justice.

The proposed intervention has the following overall objective:
"To strengthen the ability of refugees, particularly Syrians, and vulnerable Jordanians, particularly women, children and legally excluded groups, to exercise their rights and reduce legal vulnerability through gender responsive legal protection services, empowered local actors, and accessible, accountable justice institutions."
The programme is structured around three interlinked sub-objectives, each corresponding to one or more outcomes:
Sub-Objective 1: Strengthening access to reliable legal information and referral services for refugees and vulnerable Jordanians, particularly women, by enhancing the capacity of local organisations and community-based actors through coordinated capacity strengthening, knowledge sharing, and system-level improvements. This sub-objective is expected to deliver two outcomes: (1.1) improved knowledge and understanding of legal rights and available remedies among refugees and vulnerable Jordanians, particularly women; and (1.2) strengthened capacity of community-based organisations to effectively deliver legal information and referral services to refugees and vulnerable Jordanians.
Sub-Objective 2: Enhance access to justice for refugees and vulnerable Jordanians by delivering targeted legal counselling, assistance and evidence-based policy engagement that address complex documentation, civil status, housing, land and property, and return-related legal challenges, with a focus on women and legally excluded groups. This sub-objective is expected to deliver two outcomes: (2.1) refugees and vulnerable Jordanians obtain or exercise their rights through legal aid support; and (2.2) policies, practices or behaviours are positively influenced through evidence-based advocacy and engagement.
Sub-Objective 3: Improve the accessibility and responsiveness of Jordan's justice institutions by supporting the Ministry of Justice to institutionalise, operationalise, and digitalise inclusive fast track small claims procedures and strengthen the capacity of justice actors to apply them consistently. This sub-objective is expected to deliver one outcome: (3.1) improved efficiency and accessibility of the Jordanian justice system through strengthened small-claims procedures and enhanced capacity of justice actors.
The programme's intended impact is a more accessible, inclusive, gender responsive and resilient justice ecosystem in Jordan, where refugees and vulnerable Jordanians, particularly those with heightened legal vulnerability, experience strengthened protection, reduced legal insecurity, and improved pathways towards durable solutions.
